mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points over three months signals an improving labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) by more than 5% over three months signals a strengthening housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over two months signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as production efficiency and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 55% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for three consecutive months, signals a stable monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investor confidence increases.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 45% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between a decreasing unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increasing nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a robust labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp & PAYEMS increase > 100k in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 55% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between a rising real GDP (GDPC1) and a falling retail and food services sales (RSAFS) signals a shift in consumer spending patterns, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as market participants anticipate a potential economic slowdown.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increase > 1% & RSAFS decrease > 1% in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) coupled with a stable or decreasing consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals a productive yet stable inflation environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and consumer purchasing power improve.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increase > 1% & CPIAUCSL stable or decrease in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.
